why: The El Camino Kendachi plant is a fenced industrial factory in Arroyo: a street gate and yard, a main hall with production machinery, forklifts, a security outpost and Matheus Stove's upstairs office, plus a back gate and roof/back ways in. Vanilla only populates it for El Capitan's gig 'Race to the Top', when the plant's security detail, its floor workers, an outside scaffolding/cleaning crew and a yard full of cars are switched on. This proposal keeps the single quest prefab those people need and restores the plant's normal working state: the outside crew, the five floor workers and the full security detail (guards, security droids and netrunner) in their initial at-post phases. The gig's objective computer interaction, quest shard, mappins, holocalls and 20 quest-spawned yard cars stay out.

open_questions: Walk in through the main gate and the factory door: both should be shut but openable, not sealed. Vanilla force-closes and unpowers them and no gig runs to unlock them, so the runtime door policy has to power them; check the prompt and the DoorPolicy log line.

Watch the security detail for a minute: eight human guards, four security droids and the netrunner should hold their posts and not open fire on a visitor. The catalogue has no resolved spot map for #arr_03_combat_com, so its calm posture is unverified.

Walk the factory floor and the yard: five workers should be at machines or on their patrol spots and the outside crew should be kneeling/cleaning by the scaffolding, none crouched, hiding or frozen at the spawner.
Check Matheus Stove's office and its computer: no gig objective prompt, no incriminating-data interaction and no quest shard should be reachable. The office should read as a normal manager's office.
Try the back gate and the ladder door: the Body/Technical checks should still appear and work, and neither route should be the only way in or out.

Look at the entrance security: the metal detector/security system should not attack or lock the front route. The wiki says the entrance metal detector can be hacked and turned friendly; confirm it behaves normally without the gig.

Look at the yard: does it read as a working plant or an empty slab? Vanilla's 20 quest-spawned cars do not spawn without the gig, and the single community SUV #arr_03_cars_com car_001/default is not proposed here.

communities.why: The plant's whole security detail: four security droids on their start spots, eight human security guards on patrol/courtyard posts and one netrunner for the security net, all in their initial phases (droids A, humans A_spawn). Vanilla switches this whole community on when the plant is set up and only moves enemy_001/002/005 to phase B for the alert, so A/A_spawn is the pre-alert at-post state. Rule 11a keeps the combat group first, and a private Kendachi plant should have its guards on duty. The catalogue could not resolve a community-area node for this spawner, so the calm posture and the exact workspots need the tour.

The factory-floor crew: four generic sts_std_arr_03_worker entries plus the named worker_005, all in their initial A_spawn phase, with A/B spots and patrol splines around the production hall. Vanilla switches the whole community on as part of the plant's setup (worker_001's B phase belongs to the fight), so this is the plant's ordinary staff, not quest-only actors. Posture is unverified because the catalogue has no community-area node for this spawner.

The outside crew working the scaffolding: one WorkerMale whose phases A and B both use two relaxed workspots, kneeling to inspect the ground and standing at a window to clean it. Vanilla activates the community whole from the venue's open-world phase (and the district street-story phase), i.e. as part of the plant's normal look, not the fight.

proximity_wait.why: The yard's street-side main gate (DoorControllerPS, #arr_03_main_gate) is the first device on the normal way in and streams with the venue from exterior_-9_-27_0_0. The venue drives no terminal or closer interior device on the approach, so the main gate is the safest anchor.
